paragraphs: GeoCivix sells cloud-based software that cities, counties and municipalities use to run permitting, licensing, inspections, plan review and citizen services from one system. The pitch is a replacement for paper-based workflows with digital applications, automated routing, electronic plan review, mobile inspections and online payments.

Applicants use a government portal open around the clock, where they manage their projects and pay fees without calling or coming into the office. Staff mark up documents and let the system automate routing. Notifications and comment letters go back out to applicants as reviews move along. Inspectors work from a tablet or smart phone in the field, taking photos, creating reports and managing workloads on site. Permits, inspections, plans, documents, notes and approvals stay organized in one place.

Staff, reviewers, inspectors, citizens and contractors all work from the same project record. An implementation team starts by collecting application forms, communication templates, fee formulas and document workflows for configuration. The company says many agencies launch initial workflows in as little as 6 weeks, with full deployment typically completed within a few months. Every subscription is said to include unlimited technical support for all users. Listed integrations include ESRI ArcGIS, Bluebeam Revu, Cityworks, Infor/Hansen, FireRMS, Laserfiche and payment systems.

quote.text: GeoCivix offers straightforward pricing with free, unlimited support, training, and software upgrades.
